intro: Philadelphia rewards visitors with walkable colonial streets, world-class museums, and a lively food scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: SEPTA runs the subway, trolleys, and Regional Rail; fares are about $2-2.50 per ride.
Buses cover the whole city; SEPTA Key card or contactless payment works.
Taxis are metered; Uber and Lyft both operate widely.
Driving is possible but parking is costly and traffic is heavy in Center City.
Walking is easy in Center City; most sights are within 30 minutes on foot.
Bikes are popular; the Schuylkill River Trail is a favorite. RiverLink ferry runs to Camden in summer.

independence-hall.name: Independence Hall
independence-hall.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–17:00 · check on the day
independence-hall.tip: Get free timed tickets at the Independence Visitor Center early; the ranger tour is short and worth it.

liberty-bell.name: Liberty Bell
liberty-bell.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–17:00 · check on the day
liberty-bell.tip: Go right at opening or late afternoon; the line moves fast but midday is crowded.

philadelphia-museum-of-art.name: Philadelphia Museum of Art
philadelphia-museum-of-art.price_text: ≈ $30 adults · under 18 free · pay-what-you-wish first Sunday
philadelphia-museum-of-art.tip: Run the Rocky steps first, then spend the afternoon inside; the collection is huge.

adventure-aquarium.name: Adventure Aquarium
adventure-aquarium.price_text: ≈ $35–45 adults · cheaper online · check on the day
adventure-aquarium.tip: Buy tickets online and arrive at opening; it is across the river in Camden, NJ.

clementon-park.name: Clementon Park and Splash World
clementon-park.price_text: ≈ $40–55 depending on ticket type · check on the day
clementon-park.hours: Seasonal, roughly late May–early September · check on the day
clementon-park.tip: It is a 30-minute drive into New Jersey; go on a weekday and bring swim gear.

diggerland.name: Diggerland USA
diggerland.price_text: ≈ $40–50 · cheaper online · check on the day
diggerland.hours: Seasonal, roughly spring–fall · check on the day
diggerland.tip: Best for kids who love machines; it is in West Berlin, NJ, so plan a car or rideshare.

eastern-state-penitentiary.name: Eastern State Penitentiary
eastern-state-penitentiary.tip: Take the audio guide; Al Capone's cell and the crumbling cellblocks are the highlights.

funplex.name: Funplex (Mount Laurel)
funplex.price_text: ≈ $25–40 per activity pass · check on the day
funplex.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–22:00 · check on the day
funplex.tip: Indoor rides and arcades; a good rainy-day backup for families, 25 minutes from Center City.

kimmel-center.name: Kimmel Center
kimmel-center.price_text: Varies by concert · some free events
kimmel-center.hours: Box office and building roughly daily · check the day's schedule
kimmel-center.tip: Check the calendar for Philadelphia Orchestra or free lobby concerts; the glass roof is worth a look.

nude-descending.name: Nude Descending a Staircase
nude-descending.price_text: Included with Philadelphia Museum of Art admission
nude-descending.hours: Same as the museum · closed Monday
nude-descending.tip: Duchamp's painting is inside the Philadelphia Museum of Art; ask staff for the modern galleries.

philadelphia-zoo.name: Philadelphia Zoo
philadelphia-zoo.price_text: ≈ $22–28 · cheaper online · check on the day
philadelphia-zoo.tip: America's first zoo; go early when animals are active and bring water in summer.

reading-terminal-market.name: Reading Terminal Market
reading-terminal-market.hours: Roughly Mon–Sat 08:00–18:00 · Sun 09:00–17:00 · check on the day
reading-terminal-market.tip: Come hungry and go for a roast pork sandwich or a cheesesteak; cash helps at some stalls.

ritas-italian-ice.name: Rita's Italian Ice
ritas-italian-ice.hours: Varies by branch · usually daily afternoon–evening
ritas-italian-ice.tip: Order a gelati (Italian ice layered with custard); branches are all over the city.

silver-linings-playbook.name: Silver Linings Playbook
silver-linings-playbook.price_text: Free to see film locations · some are private homes
silver-linings-playbook.tip: The film is set in the Philadelphia suburbs; the Llanelli-like diner scenes and the museum steps are the easy spots to visit.

the-gross-clinic.name: The Gross Clinic
the-gross-clinic.price_text: Included with Philadelphia Museum of Art admission
the-gross-clinic.hours: Same as the museum · closed Monday
the-gross-clinic.tip: Eakins' painting hangs in the Philadelphia Museum of Art; check which gallery before you go.

university-of-pennsylvania.name: University of Pennsylvania
university-of-pennsylvania.tip: Walk Locust Walk and see College Hall; the Penn Museum is nearby if you want more.

city-hall-tower.name: Philadelphia City Hall Tower
city-hall-tower.price_text: ≈ $6–10 tower tour · check on the day
city-hall-tower.hours: Weekdays roughly 10:00–16:00 · check on the day
city-hall-tower.tip: The tower observation deck gives a close view of William Penn's statue and Broad Street.

south-street.name: South Street walk
south-street.tip: Walk from Headhouse Square to South Street for shops, murals and cheap eats.

rittenhouse-square.name: Rittenhouse Square
rittenhouse-square.tip: Sit with coffee and watch the city; the surrounding streets are good for a stroll and dinner.

schuylkill-river-trail.name: Schuylkill River Trail
schuylkill-river-trail.tip: Rent a bike or walk the river path at sunset; the skyline view from the west bank is the best free view in town.

el-freight.name: Elfreth's Alley
el-freight.price_text: Free to walk · house museum small fee
el-freight.tip: America's oldest continuously lived-in street; it is short, so pair it with Old City sights.

cheesesteak-tour.name: Cheesesteak and Old City food walk
cheesesteak-tour.hours: Tours usually late morning and afternoon
cheesesteak-tour.tip: A guided walk covers history and a cheesesteak in one go; book ahead in summer.

penn-museum.name: Penn Museum
penn-museum.tip: World archaeology with Egyptian and Mesopotamian galleries; quieter than the big museums.

styles.label: Food

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: The Barnes, the Museum of Art steps and murals all over town.

stays.why: Most central. Walk to City Hall, Reading Terminal Market and the subway; short walk or ride to Old City.
Steps from Independence Hall, the Liberty Bell and Elfreth's Alley. Quieter at night.
Leafy, upscale and full of restaurants and shops. Good base for food and shopping.
Near Penn, Drexel and the museums along the Schuylkill. Cheaper rooms, short ride to Center City.

food: Order a cheesesteak at a classic stand; ask for 'wit' or 'witout' onions. Expect about $10–15.
Reading Terminal Market: one big hall of local food stalls. Go hungry and early; it is busy at lunch.
Try a soft pretzel and water ice (Italian ice) — two cheap Philadelphia classics.
Many small restaurants are BYOB; bring your own wine and save on the bill.
Book ahead for popular dinner spots on weekends. Prices range from cheap eats to fine dining.
more_time: Add a day for the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Rocky Steps, then walk the Schuylkill River Trail.
Eastern State Penitentiary and the Barnes Foundation make a good half-day in Fairmount.
In summer, take the RiverLink ferry to Camden for the waterfront and aquarium.
